subject: Access controls and support access — follow-up from discovery call
messages:
From: Lucy Chen <lucy.chen@fintrust.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Aaron Patel <aaron.patel@fintrust.com>
Date: Thu, 20 May 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: access controls questions from today's call

Hi Marissa,

Thanks for the call this morning — appreciated the clear overview of Redwood's serving architecture and the dedicated/private deployment options. A few follow-ups from our security/privacy team around customer data access:

1) RBAC and least-privilege model: can you confirm how roles are defined at the tenant level vs. org level? We need assurance that FinTrust admins can define and limit support and engineer access strictly per-team and per-environment.

2) Support access / break-glass: what is Redwood's standard process when support engineers need to access a customer's environment for troubleshooting? Is there a time-bound approval flow and audit trail?

3) Logging and audit: what events are logged (query text, request metadata, who accessed what) and how long are logs retained? Are logs forwarded to a customer-managed SIEM?

4) Data residency and PII handling: confirm that we can restrict processing and logs to specific regions, and any PII scrubbing recommendations during troubleshooting.

Could you send a short recap and any docs/policy pages you can share? Aaron and I will prep the security questionnaire for tomorrow's legal review.

Thanks,
Lucy
Lucy Chen

Subject: Re: Follow-up: access controls questions from today's call

Hi Lucy / Aaron — great speaking with you both. Recap below and next steps. I've looped in Rishi (Head of Security Integrations) and Monica (Customer Success) for the technical + rollout items.

Quick answers (high level):
- RBAC & least privilege: Redwood supports tenant-scoped roles. Customers can create custom roles and map to SSO groups (SCIM / SAML). By default we provide admin, developer, read-only, and support roles; you can create narrower roles (e.g., "monitoring-only" that can see dashboards but not token metadata). Role bindings are enforced at the model/route level so you can restrict access to production models.
- Support access / break-glass: we have a formal break-glass flow. Support can request temporary access via the console; requests require approval from a designated FinTrust approver (can be a mailbox or an SSO group). Access is time-limited (default 2 hours) and every session is provisioned with a temporary credential. All break-glass requests generate an immutable audit record.
- Logging & audit: we log administrative events (role changes, break-glass approvals), API-level metadata (request_id, model, tokens_count, IP), and operator sessions. By default, request payloads are not stored in plaintext in the admin logs — full request/response traces are opt-in and can be routed to a customer-managed S3/GCS or forwarded to your SIEM via our log-forwarding integration. Retention is configurable per contract; default is 90 days for admin logs, 365 days for operator audit trails.
- Data residency & PII: private deployments let you pin processing to a region; hosted customers can choose region(s) for storage/processing. For troubleshooting, we recommend redacting PII before sharing prompts with support; alternatively, you can enable our masked-logging feature where sensitive fields are tokenized prior to being written to logs.

Attachments: I'm attaching the RBAC whitepaper and our support access playbook which describe the break-glass workflow and audit artifacts.

Next steps:
- Rishi: can you scope the detailed answers Lucy requested on session recording retention and the exact audit fields we capture?
- Monica: I'll coordinate a short tech review next week and share the mutual action plan template.
- Lucy/Aaron: if you can send the security questionnaire items with priority flags, we'll map answers to each item.

Happy to hop on a 30-min follow-up if helpful.

Hi Lucy — quick technical follow-up with the fields and retention details you asked for. Pasted below are the primary audit/event fields (we can provide a sample export):

- event_id
- timestamp (ISO8601)
- actor_id (SSO uid or support engineer id)
- actor_role (role at time of event)
- action (e.g., break_glass_request, break_glass_approve, role_update, api_request)
- target_resource (tenant_id / model_route)
- request_id (correlates to runtime request)
- request_metadata (model, seq_length, tokens_count, latency_ms)
- session_id (for interactive support sessions)
- session_duration_seconds
- redaction_flag (true if request payload redacted/masked)

Retention options we support (per-contract):
- 90 days (default for admin metadata)
- 365 days (extended audit trail)
- custom (customer-managed S3/GCS with lifecycle rules)

Support session access model:
- Temporary credentials are minted via the control-plane when a break-glass is approved; creds expire automatically.
- All session activity is recorded (API calls made under the session id, operator commands).
- For high-sensitivity customers, we offer a mandatory two-approver flow for any break-glass and realtime notification to a customer-owned Slack/email distribution.

On PII: we offer two paths — masked-logging (automatic tokenization of configured sensitive fields) or an opt-in full-telemetry mode where payloads are stored encrypted in customer-owned storage. We recommend masked-logging + customer-side sample export for troubleshooting whenever possible.

I'll summarize this into a short one-pager and share it to the link Marissa provided. If FinTrust wants, we can also schedule a 30-min runbook review with our SREs to walk through a mock break-glass.

—Rishi
